cells.tense: You are holding the beginning of something and it's meant to be shared.
cells.ask: Show one person what you're holding before it's finished, and let them see the first version.
cells.core:
You can feel with people and keep your own shape while you do it. There's something new taking form in your hands — a first piece, not worked yet — and you're not rushing it or hiding it. That's a real thing: you're in the room with the other person and the whole of what you're carrying both. Connection isn't costing you the direction, and the direction isn't costing you the room.

The balance holds because you don't have to force it on anyone. What you're holding can be met with someone else, and if it's not understood yet, the connection stays. Keep the piece in your hand. What you're carrying forward is the first thing, not the finished one.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding what's new and staying in the room with people.
cells.verb: holding one new piece of what will be, not yet given
cells.place: the room where you turn toward people

cells.tense: You're already living in how this will land long before it's ready to land.
cells.ask: Say where the new piece stands right now, without needing anyone to bless it or approve it.
cells.core:
You have something started, and you're living several steps ahead in how people will take it. Before it's shown, you're already hearing the response, already adjusting for a room you haven't entered. The feeling-with-people is real, but it's arriving ahead of the thing it's meant for — you're braced against what they'll think before they've seen anything.

The connection you have is worth keeping. It doesn't work when you've already spent it on a response that hasn't happened. Bring the piece to the point it's at today. Let the room answer what's here, not what you're rehearsing. The direction you're steering is yours. Choosing from what's clear now is enough.

cells.tense: You have something new in your hands and you haven't brought it to anyone.
cells.ask: Put one piece of what you're working on where someone you trust can see it, and let that be the whole of it.
cells.core:
There's something you've started — a first piece, the beginning of what you mean to build — and it's stayed behind the door with you. The connection you're capable of is there; it just isn't being spent. You've been carrying this alone longer than the piece has needed, and the easy back-and-forth with people that would keep it moving isn't happening. Feeling-with is a muscle, and it's gone quiet from lack of use.

The piece doesn't need to be finished, and nobody has to say anything wise about it. Set one thing down where another person can see it with you, and let that be the whole of the move. The room doesn't have to answer the work. It only has to be a room you're in with someone.

cells.tense: You're already reading the room for what people can take, and calling it nothing.
cells.ask: Name one way you feel toward someone as what you're choosing, not as the situation making you.
cells.core:
You're already turning toward people with the new thing in your hands. You read what they can carry, you shape how it's said, and it works — the room meets you. That reading is yours, and you've been talking as if that's just how people are, as if the care happened to you. What goes right here is you knowing what someone can hold and offering it in a way they can take.

The alignment you keep making with people is something you're doing on purpose, and it belongs to you. You could say a piece of it out loud — what you saw and what you gave — as your own move, not the room's. That's the same direction you already have in your hands, made plainly yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're doing the alignment. Call it yours.

attempts.check: The record does not say where the seed of form is going or how it will be received in this person's relationships; every cell must stay with what they're holding now, not what it becomes. A reader could reasonably say their connection to people is fine and it's the work that hasn't started — so no cell may claim the relational side is broken, only name what's held and how it's met. The asks are small acts of showing what's held; if the read is wrong about which part of life is out of step, the act is still a way to make the seed real to someone, so they stand. The sentence that serves the writer is the room finding a new strength and the asking being received; I've cut that and kept the room at the act.
